subject.title: feat(mac): Quick Chat — global-shortcut floating composer for the main session

question: Should Quick Chat automatically claim Option-Space for every existing macOS installation that has no stored Quick Chat shortcut, or should users explicitly choose the shortcut in Settings or onboarding?
rationale: The dependency explicitly discourages initial shortcuts in publicly distributed apps because they can collide with existing user workflows, while the PR intentionally presents Option-Space as an opt-out-free default; repository intent is required to accept that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Make shortcut opt-in
options.body: Remove the initial chord, keep the Settings recorder and menu item, and introduce the shortcut through an explicit user choice.

options.title: Keep Option-Space by policy
options.body: Retain the automatic default only with explicit maintainer acceptance and proof covering upgrade-time conflicts, disabling, and recorder replacement behavior.

options.title: Pause Quick Chat
options.body: Defer the feature if a safe default and discoverable opt-in flow cannot be agreed for this release.

recommendation.title: Make shortcut opt-in
recommendation.body: Remove the initial chord, keep the Settings recorder and menu item, and introduce the shortcut through an explicit user choice.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR’s maintainer label and demonstrated ownership of the macOS feature make this person the best available product-direction owner.
